name: AI invoice chaser
one_liner: Sends polite, escalating payment reminders on behalf of freelancers and small agencies so they get paid without writing awkward follow-up emails.
target_customer: Freelancers and 1-15 person agencies who invoice business clients on net terms (often from PDFs, Stripe or an invoicing app) and currently chase late payers by hand or with a basic built-in reminder.

existing_products.name: ChaseAI
existing_products.pricing: Starter from $9/month with a 14-day free trial; higher tiers exist but their prices were not visible in any indexed source.
existing_products.positioning: AI invoice chaser for freelancers: upload the invoice PDF, AI writes and sends a professional reminder sequence; no accounting-software integration required.
existing_products.strengths: Cheapest entry price found, two-minute setup, works from a PDF so it covers freelancers who invoice from Word/Canva/Stripe; publishes its own 'best invoice chasing software' comparison content for SEO.
existing_products.weaknesses: No review presence on G2/Capterra/Product Hunt found; no integrations with accounting tools; claims like 'paid 3x faster' are unsubstantiated vendor marketing.
existing_products.traction_signal: No user, revenue or review counts found; has an X account (@ChaseAiApp) and an earlier vercel.app prototype, suggesting a recent (2025-2026) solo/indie launch.

existing_products.name: RemindFox
existing_products.pricing: Free 'Scout' plan (one active chase at a time); 'Silver Fox' $19/month for unlimited simultaneous chases.
existing_products.positioning: AI-powered polite payment nudges for freelancers who hate the 'just checking in' email; up to four scheduled reminders with a 3-hour opt-out window before each send; markets itself as a Chaser HQ and Invoice Ninja alternative.
existing_products.strengths: Exactly the proposed positioning (polite, escalating, freelancer-first); free tier for trial; comparison pages targeting incumbent brand searches.
existing_products.weaknesses: Brand new (added to AlternativeTo 27 May 2026), no reviews found, unclear whether it reads client replies or just fires a fixed schedule.
existing_products.traction_signal: Listed on AlternativeTo May 2026 and in G2's discussion index; no review counts or user numbers found.

existing_products.name: Paidly (Always Paid)
existing_products.pricing: Free limited plan; paid plans between $12 and $52/month.
existing_products.positioning: Utility SaaS for freelancers and agencies that ingests invoices by email forward, PDF upload or API, sends escalating reminders in a chosen tone, and auto-marks invoices paid when payment confirmation emails are forwarded.
existing_products.strengths: No accounting-software dependency; tone and escalation customisation; AI matching of payment confirmations.
existing_products.weaknesses: Own site not indexed in results, only third-party directory listings; no reviews found; unclear if still actively developed.

existing_products.name: Paidnice
existing_products.pricing: Essentials $39/month (100 invoices actioned), Pro $69/month (250 invoices actioned); SMS charged per message (USD $0.10, GBP £0.05); free trial.
existing_products.positioning: AR automation for small and mid-sized businesses on Xero and QuickBooks Online: reminders, statements, automated late fees and interest, payment plans, escalation.
existing_products.strengths: Winner of Xero Global Small Business App of the Year 2025 and finalist in four 2026 categories; 5.0 average across 81 Xero App Store reviews (June 2026); claims 25% average DSO reduction; widest enforcement feature set at the lowest flat SMB price.
existing_products.weaknesses: Requires Xero or QuickBooks, so pure-PDF/Stripe freelancers are excluded; $39 floor is high for a solo freelancer with a handful of invoices; email-template rather than conversational AI.
existing_products.traction_signal: 'Hundreds of business owners' per its own site; 81 five-star Xero App Store reviews; award wins in 2025 and 2026.

existing_products.name: Chaser
existing_products.pricing: Compact plan £199/month (UK) or $259/month (US) for companies under £4M turnover; jumps to £599/month above that; annual or monthly billing.
existing_products.positioning: The category-defining UK credit-control platform for finance teams: automated reminders, debtor monitoring, payment portal, escalation to a debt-recovery service.
existing_products.strengths: Founded 2013, ~30 staff, est. $3.3M ARR (Latka estimate), $4-6M raised; claims $7B+ collected; 4.4 on G2; deep Xero/QBO/Sage integrations.
existing_products.weaknesses: 2026 price rise pushed the floor to £199/month, which competitor blogs (Paidnice, Trove, Equisettle) explicitly exploit; reviewers cite weak reporting and inability to reply directly to client responses inside the tool.
existing_products.traction_signal: Est. $3.3M ARR and $9.9M valuation (getlatka.com); shortlisted for three Credit Strategy Awards 2025.

existing_products.name: FreshBooks (Plus tier)
existing_products.pricing: Lite $23/month (no automated reminders), Plus $43/month (automated reminders and scheduled late fees), Premium $70/month; 30-day trial.
existing_products.positioning: All-in-one freelancer accounting where automated late-payment reminders and late fees are a paid-tier feature bundled with invoicing.
existing_products.strengths: Reminders fire from the same system that issued the invoice, so no data entry; large existing freelancer base; late fees auto-added to the next reminder.
existing_products.weaknesses: Reminders are gated behind the $43 tier; fixed templates rather than AI-written or reply-aware; single-user pricing with $11/seat add-ons.
existing_products.traction_signal: Long-established category leader for freelancer invoicing (reviewed by NerdWallet, Agiled, Jobbers 2026 lists).

existing_products.name: QuickBooks Online with Intuit Assist / Payments Agent
existing_products.pricing: Included in QuickBooks Online subscriptions (from roughly $35/month); no separate charge for the AI agents.
existing_products.positioning: Since 1 July 2025 QuickBooks ships a 'Payments Agent' that tracks invoices, analyses customer payment behaviour, drafts AI reminders and suggests late fees; Intuit claims automated reminders get businesses paid 45% faster (about 5 days sooner).
existing_products.strengths: Zero-friction for the millions of QBO users; AI-generated wording is already there; bundled free with the accounting plan.
existing_products.weaknesses: Only covers invoices raised inside QuickBooks; agents are US-first and still maturing; SMB QBO users are not the freelancer-with-PDF segment.
existing_products.traction_signal: Intuit press release and Accounting Today coverage of the July 2025 launch; QuickBooks is the largest SMB accounting platform in the US.

existing_products.name: Zoho Invoice / Wave (free invoicing with reminders)
existing_products.pricing: Zoho Invoice: free forever (500-1,000 invoices/year, 2 users) including automated payment reminders; Wave: free invoicing with automated reminders, late fees added manually.
existing_products.positioning: Free invoicing suites that include scheduled reminders as a checkbox feature.
existing_products.strengths: Free, widely recommended in every 2026 freelancer invoicing listicle, reminders trigger from the invoice record.
existing_products.weaknesses: Template-only, fixed schedules, no tone escalation or reply handling; 'Powered by Zoho' branding on free tier.
existing_products.traction_signal: Zoho and Wave are among the most-cited freelancer invoicing tools across NerdWallet, Agiled and Jobbers 2026 rankings.

existing_products.name: Manual chasing, Google Sheets scripts, or a virtual assistant
existing_products.pricing: Gumroad 'Invoice Reminder Pro' Google Sheets automations sell for one-off fees; Upwork accounts-receivable freelancers charge $22-42/hour; most freelancers simply write the email themselves.
existing_products.positioning: The default workaround: hand-written follow-ups, a spreadsheet with a script that emails overdue rows daily, or paying a bookkeeper/VA to chase.
existing_products.strengths: Free or cheap, fully under the freelancer's control, no new tool to learn.
existing_products.weaknesses: Awkward, inconsistent, easy to forget; agencies report 3-10+ hours per month chasing (Ignition 2025).
existing_products.traction_signal: Multiple Gumroad sheet-automation products and 88 GitHub repositories matching 'invoice reminder freelancer' show people building their own.

demand_signals: Ignition's April 2025 survey of 273 US agency leaders (mostly 1-50 staff): 97% regularly deal with late client payments, 71% say at least one in four invoices is late, 84% spend 3-10+ hours a month chasing.

Intuit QuickBooks 2025 Small Business Late Payments Report (2,487 US businesses <100 employees, January 2025): 56% are owed money on unpaid invoices, average $17,500 outstanding, nearly 3 in 10 owners have delayed paying themselves.

Remote's 2025 Contractor Management Report: 85% of freelancers are paid late at least sometimes and 21% are paid late or not at all more than half the time; IPSE 2025 UK survey: 71% of freelancers have experienced late payment, average overdue invoice sits 23 days past due.

A cluster of tiny freelancer-focused reminder tools launched in 2025-2026 (ChaseAI, RemindFox, Chasa, Landolio, Reminvo, PayMeSwift, Invoice Chase iOS) plus Gumroad Google Sheets automations and 88 GitHub repos for 'invoice reminder freelancer' show people are building and selling workarounds.

Competitor blogs (Paidnice, Trove, Equisettle, RemindFox) all publish 'Chaser alternatives' pages targeting people priced out by Chaser's 2026 rise to £199/month, and Hacker News and Indie Hackers threads repeatedly ask how freelancers ensure clients pay.

Regulation is being written for this problem: UK government announced a 60-day statutory payment cap, mandatory 8%+base-rate late interest and new Small Business Commissioner powers in March 2026 (phased in later 2026); California SB-988 (effective 1 Jan 2025) makes late-paying clients liable for double the amount owed to freelancers.

market.size_estimate: Own bottom-up estimate: roughly 2-4 million freelancers and micro-agencies in the US and UK who invoice business clients on net terms regularly enough to pay for chasing; at a blended $12-15/month that is a theoretical $300M-700M/year serviceable market, of which the realistic obtainable slice for a bootstrapped tool is low single-digit millions (Chaser, the UK category leader at 10x the price point, is only an estimated $3.3M ARR after 12 years). Top-down, the whole accounts-receivable automation software market is about $4.0B in 2025 growing to ~$8.3B by 2030 (researchandmarkets), but 59% of that spend is large enterprise.
market.sizing_method: Bottom-up: Upwork Research Institute (2025) says 1 in 4 US skilled knowledge workers work independently; I assumed only ~10-15% of them plus small agencies (Ignition/Demand Gen Report: tens of thousands of 1-50 person US agencies) invoice B2B on terms often enough to buy a chasing tool, then multiplied by comparable pricing ($9 ChaseAI, $19 RemindFox, $39-69 Paidnice). Cross-checked against Chaser's estimated $3.3M ARR and Paidnice's 'hundreds' of customers as evidence of what small players actually capture.
market.growth: Growing: freelance participation is rising (Google Trends interest in 'start freelancing' up ~235% over five years per Kaplan), late payment is worsening (MediaPost/Ignition 2025), AR automation market CAGR is ~15% with SMEs the fastest-growing segment (~12% CAGR per Mordor), and new UK/California legislation is raising awareness. The counter-trend is that reminder functionality is being absorbed for free into QuickBooks, Xero, Zoho and Wave.

monetisation.payer: The freelancer or agency owner (the creditor), paying out of pocket; possibly bookkeepers/accountants buying on behalf of clients.
monetisation.model: Monthly subscription, tiered by number of active chases or invoices monitored, with a free tier for one active chase; a per-invoice or success-fee variant (Anchor charges a flat $5 only when money moves) is a possible alternative but harder to meter without payment rails.
monetisation.price_point: $12-19/month for solo freelancers (between ChaseAI $9 and RemindFox $19), $39-49/month for agencies with multiple clients and team seats (just under Paidnice Essentials $39 and FreshBooks Plus $43).
monetisation.comparable_pricing: ChaseAI $9/mo; RemindFox free / $19/mo; Paidly $12-52/mo; Paidnice $39 / $69/mo; Trove £45/mo; FreshBooks Plus $43/mo (reminders included); Chaser £199 / $259/mo; Upflow ~$440/mo; Kolleno from $650/user/mo (turnover-gated). Free substitutes: Zoho Invoice, Wave, Landolio, QuickBooks' bundled Payments Agent.
monetisation.acquisition_and_serving_costs: Serving cost is near zero (LLM calls for a few emails per invoice plus transactional email at fractions of a cent). Acquisition is the problem: the need is episodic (a freelancer only cares when a client is late), so churn after the first collected invoice will be high; SEO terms are contested by a dozen content-heavy micro-competitors and incumbent blogs; paid ads at a $12/mo ARPU are unlikely to pay back. Email deliverability (SPF/DKIM/DMARC, sub-0.3% spam complaints under Gmail's 2024-2025 sender rules) is an ongoing operational cost, and Google OAuth verification for sending from the user's own Gmail adds a $540-1,000+ CASA assessment and 4-8 weeks if that route is chosen.

build.mvp_scope: Web app where a user forwards or uploads an invoice (PDF/email), the LLM extracts client, amount and due date, the user picks a tone and escalation cadence, and the system sends 3-5 scheduled reminder emails from a verified sending domain with reply-to set to the user; pause/stop when the user marks paid or when a client reply is detected; a dashboard of open chases; Stripe billing with a free single-chase tier. Optional v1.1: Xero/QuickBooks read-only sync and Stripe Invoicing webhook so invoices appear automatically.
build.effort_estimate: 3-6 weeks of evenings/weekends for the core (auth, upload, LLM extraction, scheduler, transactional email, billing) for a full-stack developer using Nuxt/Next + Postgres + a hosted LLM + Postmark/Resend + Stripe; another 3-4 weeks for a Xero or QuickBooks OAuth integration and app-store certification if pursued.

dependencies.name: LLM API (OpenAI/Anthropic) for invoice extraction and reminder wording
Transactional email provider (Postmark/Resend/SES) with domain authentication under Gmail/Yahoo bulk-sender rules
Gmail API send-as-user OAuth (sensitive scope; verification and possible CASA assessment)
Xero and QuickBooks Online APIs and app-store listing approval
Stripe for billing and optional Stripe Invoicing webhooks
SMS provider (Twilio) if SMS escalation is added

usage_frequency: Episodic for solo freelancers (only while an invoice is overdue, a few times a year); closer to monthly for agencies with a rolling book of 10-50 invoices, which is where any recurring subscription revenue would come from.
distribution_channels: SEO on long-tail 'polite payment reminder email template' / 'how to chase an unpaid invoice' queries and 'X alternative' pages: reachable but already worked by RemindFox, Landolio, ChaseAI, Paidnice, Trove and Chaser's own blog.

Xero App Store and QuickBooks App Store listings: concentrated buyer intent but requires an integration plus certification, and Paidnice already owns the category with 81 five-star reviews and two award cycles.

Freelancer communities (r/freelance, r/graphic_design, Indie Hackers, Hacker News 'Ask HN' invoicing threads, Facebook agency-owner groups): responsive to a founder story but hostile to self-promotion and small in conversion.
Product Hunt and AlternativeTo launches for an initial spike (RemindFox and ChaseAI took this route in 2026).
Bookkeeper and accountant referral partnerships (each serves dozens of freelancers/agencies): high leverage but slow to build without a network.
Integration marketplaces beyond accounting: Stripe App Marketplace, Bonsai/HoneyBook/Notion template ecosystems where freelancers already invoice.
differentiation_angles: Reply-aware chasing: read the client's reply ('will pay Friday', 'invoice disputed', 'wrong PO'), pause or reschedule the sequence and draft the human response; Chaser reviewers complain about reply handling and most micro-tools fire a fixed schedule. Copyable, but it is the one angle that improves with data on outcomes.

Source-agnostic ingestion (forwarded email, PDF, Stripe, Bonsai, Notion) rather than requiring Xero/QBO, targeting freelancers who never adopt accounting software; ChaseAI and Paidly already do this, so it is table stakes rather than a moat.

Agency mode: one account chasing on behalf of many clients under the agency's brand, with escalation to the owner and a jurisdiction-aware late-interest calculator (UK 8%+base statutory interest, California SB-988 double damages) that turns the new legislation into copy in the reminder.

Outcome data compounding: tracking which tone/cadence gets which client type to pay could become a modest proprietary dataset, but only at a scale a bootstrapped solo founder is unlikely to reach before incumbents with millions of invoices (Intuit, Xero JAX) do the same.
why_now: LLMs make reply-aware, tone-adjusted chasing cheap to build, and 2026 legislation (UK 60-day cap and statutory interest; California SB-988 double damages) is raising awareness. Against that, QuickBooks (July 2025) and Xero (Xerocon 2026) have already shipped or announced AI reminder agents, so the window for a standalone tool is closing rather than opening.
kill_risks: Incumbent absorption: QuickBooks shipped an AI Payments Agent that drafts reminders on 1 July 2025 and Xero's JAX announced predictive 'payment follow-ups' in 2026; FreshBooks, Zoho (free) and Wave (free) already include scheduled reminders. Check whether Xero's JAX follow-ups are generally available on Starter/Standard plans by early 2027; if so, the accounting-software-user segment is closed.

Direct clones already exist at $0-19/month (ChaseAI, RemindFox, Paidly, Landolio, Chasa) with the identical 'polite AI reminders for freelancers' pitch; verify via AlternativeTo/Product Hunt whether any of them reach hundreds of paying users, which would show the wedge is real but taken, or whether they stall, which would show demand at this price is too thin.

Episodic need and churn: the product is only valuable while an invoice is overdue; a 30-60 day cohort retention check on the first 50 users will reveal whether ARPU x lifetime can ever exceed acquisition cost. Freelancer SaaS comparables (Bonsai, HoneyBook) had to bundle contracts, proposals and payments to hold users.

Deliverability and platform gating: sending on a user's behalf either lands in spam from a shared domain (Gmail's 2024-2025 sender rules require SPF/DKIM/DMARC and <0.3% complaints) or requires Google OAuth verification with a CASA assessment for gmail.send; a single spam-flag incident on a shared sending domain would degrade every customer at once.

Distribution saturation: the Xero App Store slot is held by Paidnice (award winner 2025, finalist 2026) and the SEO long tail is occupied by six or more content-heavy competitors, so reaching the first hundred paying customers may cost more than they are worth at $12-19/month.
recent_moves: Intuit launched a virtual team of AI agents inside QuickBooks on 1 July 2025 including a Payments Agent that tracks invoices, drafts overdue reminders and suggests late fees (Intuit press release; Accounting Today).
Xero announced at Xerocon 2026 that JAX will predict when customers pay and automatically send payment follow-ups, part of a push to automate 'unbillable' admin (Accounting Today; TechRepublic).

Chaser raised its entry price in 2026 to £199/month (Compact, under £4M turnover) with the next tier at £599, opening room below it that Paidnice, Trove and Equisettle immediately targeted with 'Chaser alternative' pages.
Paidnice won Xero Global Small Business App of the Year 2025 and was named a finalist in four Xero Global App Awards 2026 categories.
RemindFox (May 2026), ChaseAI, Chasa and Landolio all launched freelancer-specific AI/automated reminder tools in the last ~12 months.

UK government announced (March 2026) a statutory 60-day payment cap, automatic 8%+base-rate late interest and new Small Business Commissioner enforcement powers, phasing in later in 2026; the Fair Payment Code replaced the Prompt Payment Code in December 2024.
Anchor raised a $15M seed (TechCrunch) for autonomous billing and collections for professional-services firms, charging $5 per payment instead of a subscription.

problem_severity.rationale: Frequent and costly with people already paying to cope: Ignition 2025 (n=273) 97% chase late payments and 84% spend 3-10+ hours a month; QuickBooks 2025 (n=2,487) average $17,500 owed; AR virtual assistants at $22-42/hour. Regulation targets payers, not chasing budgets, so short of 5.

market_size.rationale: Serviceable segment is the agent's own bottom-up estimate ($300-700M theoretical at $12-15/month), but observable capture is small: Chaser ~$3.3M ARR after 12 years, Paidnice 'hundreds' of customers. Fits the $10-100M realistic band.

competition.rationale: Free incumbents (QuickBooks, Xero, Zoho, Wave, FreshBooks Plus) cover accounting-software users and five-plus $0-19 clones cover PDF freelancers; only reply-aware chasing for freelancers outside accounting software is visibly underserved. Pricing corroborated across two or more snippets each.

differentiation.rationale: As stated, polite escalating AI reminders are a feature Intuit and Xero have shipped and RemindFox and ChaseAI replicate; reply-aware chasing would be a 3 but is not in the idea as written and is equally copyable.

monetisation.rationale: Clear payer and abundant comparables ($9-69/month) corroborated across snippets, but squeezed between free substitutes and an episodic need; no retention data for freelancer-tier tools.

retention.rationale: Freelancers only need it while an invoice is late (episodic), but agencies with a rolling invoice book have a monthly need; Bonsai and HoneyBook had to bundle to hold freelancers. No retention figures found for any comparable, so this is inference.

feasibility.rationale: Weeks of work on a standard stack (upload, LLM extraction, scheduler, transactional email, Stripe); the medium-risk Gmail OAuth and Xero/QBO dependencies can be deferred past launch. MVP scope and dependencies are listed; effort is the agent's estimate.

distribution.rationale: Every channel exists but is saturated: Paidnice holds the Xero App Store slot with 81 five-star reviews, six-plus competitors own the SEO long tail, and the founder has no audience or accountant network.

founder_fit.rationale: No founder profile filled in; scored as an adequate-fit solo full-stack developer with no stated domain network or interest.

timing_and_risk.rationale: The incumbents have announced and shipped this: Intuit's Payments Agent (press release, 1 July 2025) and Xero's JAX follow-ups (Accounting Today, Xerocon 2026). LLM cost and 2026 legislation are real enabling shifts, but with no mitigation for incumbent absorption this sits at the anchor-2 wording.

confidence_rationale: Every vendor, review-site and news domain (chaserhq.com, paidnice.com, chaseai.app, remindfox.net, G2, Capterra, Xero App Store, Intuit, TechRepublic, gov.uk, etc.) was blocked by the network egress proxy, so no pricing page or review page was opened directly; only GitHub loaded. Prices were instead corroborated across two or more independent search snippets each (vendor pricing pages, competitor comparison blogs by Paidnice/Trove/Equisettle, and Capterra/GetApp/SpotSaaS captures), which is reasonable but unverified. Chaser's ARR is a Latka estimate, ChaseAI/RemindFox/Paidly traction is unknown, and the market size is my own bottom-up estimate.

calibration_notes: founder_fit_and_risk: 2 -> 3. Raised 2 to 3: the rationale's 'external risk' is incumbents bundling AI reminders, which is already penalised under competition and differentiation; the remaining platform risks (Gmail OAuth, deliverability) are manageable, matching the anchor-3 wording.

Rubric v2 comparative scoring pass (ten criteria, evidence grades). Researcher scores under the old eight-criterion rubric were: problem_severity=4, market_size=3, competition=2, differentiation=1, monetisation=3, feasibility=4, distribution=2, founder_fit_and_risk=3.
timing_and_risk: 3 -> 2 in the comparative pass; see rationale.
